outlooks.text: The Abu Dhabi round on Nov 10-11 ending without a ceasefire deal
outlooks.why: Euronews reports the two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with no breakthrough on a ceasefire or on territory. The only agreement was in principle, on a prisoner exchange. AP, carried by PBS, also reports no major breakthrough.

outlooks.text: A US-Iran agreement to reopen Hormuz within the next three weeks
Fighting and cross-border strikes continuing along the Lahj front toward Aden
outlooks.why: Reuters, Al Jazeera and AP all report Houthi advances and Saudi-backed reinforcements on the Lahj front, with Tur al-Baha about 80 km from Aden.

outlooks.text: The UN announcing a date and venue for talks with the RSF-allied bloc by end of November
The Abu Dhabi round on Nov 10-11 is likely to take place, because the Kremlin and the US envoy both confirm it, though no comprehensive deal is on the table.
outlooks.why: Euronews and AP (via PBS) report that the Abu Dhabi talks took place over two days and ended with a prisoner-exchange agreement but no comprehensive deal.

outlooks.text: Houthi forces reaching Aden's outskirts in the next three weeks looks unlikely, since fighting is still reported around Tur al-Bahah, 80 km out, under coalition air raids.
A deal that reopens Hormuz within two weeks looks unlikely: Iran attaches conditions, and Trump is still floating strikes on nuclear sites.
outlooks.why: CBS News live coverage on Nov 18 reports no US-Iran agreement. Iran's offer to reopen the strait within two days still depends on its seven conditions, and mediation by Qatar continues.

outlooks.text: The Abu Dhabi round going ahead on Nov 10-11 is likely; both sides have confirmed delegations or contacts with the US envoys.
outlooks.why: Euronews reports that Russia and Ukraine held two days of talks in Abu Dhabi with US mediators. AP, via PBS, describes it as the first meeting in nine months.

outlooks.text: A larger US strike on Iran within four weeks is a roughly even chance: Trump signals one, but midterm losses add pressure against it.
Houthi forces entering Aden's outskirts in the next two to four weeks is unlikely, given government reports that the advance near Tur al-Bahah was blocked.
The Arakan Army taking Sittwe within four weeks is unlikely, though Reuters says it has neared the city.
Large Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy grid continue through the planned Abu Dhabi round.
outlooks.why: Russia-Ukraine-US talks opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, per Anadolu. Large Russian strikes continued: France 24 reported blackouts, three damaged Kyiv bridges and at least seven deaths in the capital around 20-21 November.

outlooks.text: Limited US-Iran exchanges around Qeshm and Hormuz continue while Qatar-mediated talks go on.
outlooks.why: Al Jazeera reported tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes and an Iranian claim of a downed US drone over Hormuz on 21 November. Iran also claimed a drone downing near Qeshm.

outlooks.text: Houthi missile or drone fire toward Saudi cities continues over the next two weeks.
outlooks.why: Al Jazeera reports the Saudi-led coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh. It was the third night in a row with alerts in the capital. France 24 and AFP also reported Houthi strikes on Riyadh.

outlooks.text: Military air strikes in Rakhine continue as the army's offensive to retake the state goes on.
outlooks.why: The Irrawaddy reported that regime air strikes killed over a dozen civilians in Rakhine in the past week. It said the Arakan Army is pushing toward Sittwe and Kyaukphyu. The Diplomat and others also describe an ongoing air campaign there.

outlooks.text: The Abu Dhabi round is likely to go ahead on Nov 10-11, since both Moscow and Washington have confirmed delegations; past rounds produced prisoner swaps but no deal.
outlooks.why: The round went ahead, and Euronews reports it produced an agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but no ceasefire or territorial deal. That matches the call as written.

outlooks.text: A deal to reopen Hormuz in the next few weeks looks unlikely, since Iran's army ties reopening to US concessions and no mediation outcome is reported.
Further Saudi-Houthi strikes are likely in the coming weeks, given the Nov 8 exchange and Houthi pressure near Aden; a truce would change this.
The Abu Dhabi round is likely to go ahead with modest results, given both delegations are named and Moscow says it offers no new concessions.
outlooks.why: The round took place and, per AP (via PBS), ended with a large prisoner exchange confirmed by both sides but no major breakthrough. The Moscow Times says neither side has shown major compromise.

outlooks.text: A resumption of large-scale US strikes on Iran in the next two weeks is unlikely, based on Trump's stated position, though talks remain stuck.
Further Houthi missile fire at Saudi cities is likely, given repeated launches and Houthi vows to punish Saudi Arabia.
The Abu Dhabi round ends without a general ceasefire, given Putin's stated rejection of a halt and Zelenskyy's refusal to cede land.
Hormuz traffic stays well below pre-war levels, with the US blockade in place and Iran tying talks to its conditions.
Houthi missile and drone fire at Saudi cities and energy sites continues, with no truce talks reported.
A deal settling territory in the next four weeks is very unlikely, as Russia still demands all of Donbas and Ukraine refuses to cede land.
Further ship incidents near Hormuz in the next two weeks are likely, given this week's reports and stalled talks.
More Houthi missile or drone launches at Saudi territory in the next two weeks are likely, with no de-escalation arrangement announced.
Further US air strikes in Somalia within a month are likely, given strikes in October and this week.
More drone strikes on civilian areas in the next two weeks are very likely, as UN data show drones as the main cause of child casualties.
A large prisoner exchange takes place in the coming weeks; Russian state media put it at two to three weeks.
The US and Iran agree terms to reopen Hormuz within four weeks, given Iran's denial of talks and its list of conditions.
Houthi missile and drone launches toward Saudi Arabia continue over the next two weeks, as they have for several days running.
A new round of Ukraine talks with European representatives present is held.
Further Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries are reported.
New Houthi missile or drone launches at Saudi Arabia are reported.
The US and Iran agree terms that reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
AFRICOM announces at least one more strike in Somalia.
The Nov 19 Shenzhen meeting takes place without a signed agreement on Iran or Hormuz.
outlooks.why: The Shenzhen meeting among Trump, Xi and Putin took place on Nov 19. Iranwire reports the joint declaration made no mention of Iran or the Strait of Hormuz, and other outlets report no agreement on Iran came out of it.

outlooks.text: A talks round with European representatives present is held before Dec 5.
The Houthis claim at least one further missile or drone strike on Saudi territory by Nov 28.
Fighting in Kordofan continues with no agreed ceasefire by Nov 30.
Reporting points to Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy grid continuing through the next three weeks, as Russia's defence ministry says it intends.
Iran's forces claim at least one more strike on a US-linked site in the Gulf before Dec 1.
Houthi forces reach Aden's outskirts by Dec 1; reported gains are far from the city and government forces say they are repelling attacks.
AFRICOM reports further air strikes on al-Shabaab by Dec 6, in line with its October and November pace.
Fighting in Kordofan continues without both sides agreeing to UN-led talks by Dec 6.
Further Iranian attacks or claimed attacks on Gulf shipping or Gulf bases are reported by Nov 30.
Houthi missiles or drones are again reported aimed at Saudi territory by Nov 30.
The Nov 19 Shenzhen meeting ends without a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire announcement.
Another drone hit on a merchant ship in Romanian waters is reported by Nov 30.
Both sides report further long-range strikes on bridges, energy or transport by Dec 1 while talks continue.
Iran claims at least one more drone or missile attack on a site used by US forces in the Gulf by Dec 1.
Houthi forces enter Aden city itself by Dec 1.
New drone strikes killing civilians in Kordofan or Darfur are reported by Dec 1.
AFRICOM reports at least one more strike in Somalia by Dec 15.
Further Iranian attacks on Gulf sites hosting US forces are reported by Dec 2.
Road traffic across the Kerch bridge remains suspended on Dec 2.
Houthi forces reach Aden's outskirts or cut one of its main road links by Dec 2.
Ukraine strikes the Crimea bridge or Russian refineries again by Dec 10, based on three bridge strikes in a week and an ongoing refinery campaign.

outlooks.text: UKMTO or Gulf states report another attack on shipping or on a US-hosting Gulf state by Dec 10, based on this week's repeated attacks.
Saudi or coalition officials report another Houthi missile or drone launch at Saudi territory by Dec 10, based on repeated attacks since September.
Both the army and the RSF confirm attendance at UN-set talks by Dec 19, given the in-absentia death sentence for Hemedti and ongoing Kordofan fighting.
Further Russian mass strikes on Ukrainian energy or transport infrastructure are reported in the next two weeks.
A large joint US-Israeli strike campaign on Iranian nuclear sites begins before Dec 20.
More Houthi missile or drone launches toward Saudi Arabia are reported in the next two weeks.
A Black Sea maritime ceasefire is agreed by Russia and Ukraine.
AFRICOM reports further air strikes in Somalia within two weeks.
Further Russian mass strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy sites within two weeks, since Moscow rules out limited ceasefires.
Houthi missile or drone fire at Saudi territory continues over the next two weeks, given nightly launches and coalition strikes.
The US and Iran agree terms to reopen Hormuz within two weeks, given Iran's seven conditions and Trump calling the offer fake.
